scope: Original RGB and fixed rough-ROI review only. No inference, new ROI, mask, exact-corner label, hidden-cut path or template ground truth. Visibility assessments are qualitative.
reviewExposure: Reviewer previously selected these ROIs and drafted labels for two photos. This review re-inspected original RGB rather than algorithm masks or crop overlays; not a blinded independent review.
summary: All four have substantial exposed lower edges and tips. The pale printed checker is the clearest visible-evidence crop failure. Red/green has a hidden notch; tree has clipped/occluded lobes despite visible lower runs/notch; painted basket has visible but stepped/warped edges and a shallow notch. None establishes a cutting/solver failure because these rows stop at crop resolution.

verification.rootVisualReview: All four frozen-ROI RGB previews inspected; source observations agree with the review. No exact corners, material masks or hidden cutting paths inferred.

lowerLeftEdge.observation: Red lower strip edge is exposed against blue cloth. A short fold/step and pale backing near the bottom split the apparent contour; the long edge run is available.

lowerRightEdge.observation: Green lower side and the bottom tip are exposed. Narrow backing/second-layer edges run beside the main face; gold contents do not cover these lower edges.

notch.observation: Ribbon crosses the cleft/upper meeting area. The exact body notch underneath is not directly observable; an eyelet and gold contents add nearby non-body edges.

flatOverlapSquare.observation: Visible low-count woven front has approximately straight crossing boundaries and two lower edge runs. Mild paper curvature/backing misalignment make an exact common plane uncertain; obscured notch prevents direct four-corner confirmation.

findings.diagnosis: Failure is not explained by absent lower edges or a missing selection. It combines useful visible edge evidence with a genuinely hidden notch and a non-ideal outline. A precise full-lobe/square fit cannot be claimed from the source alone.

pipelineFailure.reason: Could not identify both exposed lower paper edges. Try a rough selection around one complete heart.

lowerLeftEdge.observation: A long gold/pale lower edge runs diagonally to the bottom tip against the darker cloth. Ribbon covers the upper-left lobe/shoulder, while most of this lower straight run is exposed; needles are nearby.

lowerRightEdge.observation: The long lower-right gold/pale edge approaching the tip is exposed against cloth. The original frame clips the upper/right lobe, not the bottom tip or most of this lower run.

notch.observation: The meeting of the pale upper lobe edge and gold lobe is visible. A gold handle rises immediately behind it and merges in color, but the center is not covered by the wide ribbon.

flatOverlapSquare.observation: A projective overlap quadrilateral is plausible for the woven front. Raised branch tips, paper bowing and strong oblique shading make exact coplanarity uncertain. A complete flat-heart lobe outline is not observable because of source clipping and ribbon occlusion.

findings.diagnosis: There is real missing/occluded lobe evidence, but the reported inability to find both exposed lower edges is not a literal absence of both edge runs. The source supports an uncertain lower-edge-driven proposal, not certification of an exact complete heart model.

pipelineFailure.reason: Could not identify both exposed lower paper edges. Try a rough selection around one complete heart.

lowerLeftEdge.observation: Long diagonal lower-left edge is visible against the pale background, aided by a narrow dark edge/cast shadow. A thin pink backing/strip-end line makes the precise contour locally ambiguous.

lowerRightEdge.observation: Long diagonal lower-right edge and tip are visible. Pale blue/white paper approaches the background brightness, so the boundary is weaker than internal printed checks.

notch.observation: Both lobe contours converge at a shallow visible cleft. The pink patterned handle meets that area and makes an exact pixel coordinate uncertain; it does not erase all notch evidence.

flatOverlapSquare.observation: A near-frontal regular checker front and two long lower sides are visible. Mild paper curvature and strip offsets remain, but no large perspective/occlusion conflict prevents an approximate square model.

findings.diagnosis: Clearest failure on available visible evidence, rather than unavoidable ambiguity or an inadequate ROI. Exact corner/contact ground truth remains unannotated; source-only review cannot identify the failing internal code stage.

pipelineFailure.reason: Could not identify both exposed lower paper edges. Try a rough selection around one complete heart.

lowerLeftEdge.observation: Lower-left paper edge is exposed against dark/pink clothing. Individual protruding strip ends form small steps instead of one perfectly straight silhouette line.

lowerRightEdge.observation: Lower-right edge and bottom tip are visible against clothing; a narrow pale backing edge and curvature produce adjacent edge candidates. The caption starts below the tip and does not hide it.

notch.observation: Yellow/orange left lobe meets the magenta right lobe in a shallow upper cleft. Painted colors and a front/back paper offset make it less like a clean V, but it is not covered by the cord or a hand.

flatOverlapSquare.observation: A low-count checker overlap is recognizable. Hanging pose, bowed paper, stepped strip ends and layer offsets make a strict single flat outline less credible than for the pale checker. They do not establish an irregular interior-cutout design.

findings.diagnosis: Useful lower-edge and shallow-notch evidence exists. Failure is plausibly sensitivity to painted texture, similar-colored background and departures from perfectly straight edges, not lack of a selected complete body. This is an observation-based hypothesis, not a verified implementation root cause.

nextDiagnostic: Separate physical-paper segmentation from lower-edge sampling and shape-model rejection using fixed originals and ROIs. The pale printed checker is the clearest available-evidence case. It must still pass full template reconstruction after any crop improvement.
